answer: Each agent must lock a refundable stake before its identity becomes a vertex in the market’s trust graph; tasks are assigned only after peers validate its outputs, and a random audit slashes the stake when collusion or fabricated work is proven. Creating a thousand Sybils therefore requires a thousand separate deposits, while recycled identities have no reputation. The attacker pays real capital and loses it on one detected lie, whereas honest agents recover their stake and earn nectar or pearl rewards.
